headline: Leaving Verizon Dollars forfeits your balance and fee-free upgrades
tldr: Verizon's loyalty terms now spell out the cost of opting out: your Verizon Dollars are forfeited on the spot, and fee-free activations and upgrades end.
who: Verizon postpaid mobile, Home Internet and Fios customers enrolled in Verizon Dollars, Verizon's loyalty program, especially anyone who joined for the waived activation and upgrade fees or the Glance lock-screen rewards and is thinking of leaving
seo_title: Opting out of Verizon Dollars: you forfeit your balance and lose waived activation and upgrade fees
seo_desc: Verizon added section 7.4 to its Verizon Dollars terms: un-enrolling forfeits accumulated Dollars (except Verizon Visa Card earnings), voids refunds on items bought with Dollars and ends waived activation and upgrade fees.

redline.after: If you choose to opt out of Verizon Dollars, you agree: All accumulated Verizon Dollars will be immediately forfeited, with the exception of Verizon Dollars earned by Verizon Visa Card holders for eligible Verizon Visa Card spend.
redline.label: Verizon Dollars Terms · 7.4 Opt-Out
redline.note: Leaving the program now costs you whatever balance you haven't spent.

redline.after: You will lose access to waived fees for mobile device activations and/or upgrades.
redline.label: Verizon Dollars Terms · 7.4 Opt-Out
redline.note: Verizon's own newsroom puts those fees at up to $40 per device.

redline.after: Verizon purchases (e.g., accessories, devices) made with Verizon Dollars will be ineligible for a refund.
redline.label: Verizon Dollars Terms · 7.4 Opt-Out

actions: Before you opt out, spend your balance in the My Verizon app (Me tab, Verizon Dollars tile) on a gift card, accessory or device you want
If you bought something with Verizon Dollars and might return it, return it before you opt out: after that it can't be refunded
If you only want to stop the Glance lock-screen tracking, uninstall Glance instead of leaving Verizon Dollars; you keep your balance and the fee waivers
what:
Verizon has added a new section 7.4, "Opt-Out," to the Terms and Conditions of Verizon Dollars, the loyalty program that pays 3% of your monthly bill back in Verizon Dollars. It wasn't on the page on November 13; it is on November 14.

The section says you can unenroll "at any time via the opt-out link in the Verizon Dollars dashboard in the My Verizon App," but that if you do, "you agree" to four things:

- "All accumulated Verizon Dollars will be immediately forfeited, with the exception of Verizon Dollars earned by Verizon Visa Card holders for eligible Verizon Visa Card spend."
- "You will no longer earn Verizon Dollars for Verizon bill payments or other eligible offers like Lock Screen Rewards through Glance, if applicable."
- "Verizon purchases (e.g., accessories, devices) made with Verizon Dollars will be ineligible for a refund."
- "You will lose access to waived fees for mobile device activations and/or upgrades."

It adds that leaving "will not affect hotel or ticket rewards you have already redeemed" and that you "may re-enroll in the Program at any time via the My Verizon App." The terms don't say whether re-enrolling restores a forfeited balance.

## Why it matters

The waived fees are the main reason many customers joined. Verizon's newsroom post launching the program called it "the end of Device Upgrade and Activation fees" and put them at "up to $40 in fees per device," available only to customers who opt in. Section 7.4 makes clear the waiver lasts only as long as you stay enrolled. The terms already said Dollars are forfeited if you cancel Verizon service (7.3) or if Verizon ends your enrollment (7.2); now opting out of the program alone costs you the balance too.

It also matters for the Glance deal we covered on October 19: earning $5 a month in Lock Screen Rewards requires keeping "Do not sell or share my personal information" switched off. Customers who regret that and want out of Verizon Dollars entirely now see in writing that leaving forfeits what they earned. Uninstalling the Glance app ends Lock Screen Rewards without leaving Verizon Dollars, according to section 10.2.

What stays the same: you earn 3% of eligible bill payments, Dollars earned without a Verizon Visa Card still expire 12 months after they're issued, and Visa cardholders keep card-earned Dollars after opting out.

Verizon's Verizon Dollars FAQ (checked Nov 14) lists the same consequences under "Can I un-enroll from Verizon Dollars?" We don't know when that FAQ answer was added. The terms page still shows a placeholder, "effective as of <DATE>," so there is no stated effective date.
sources: Verizon Dollars Program: Terms and Conditions
About Verizon: Verizon breaks industry mold (loyalty program launch)
faq: What happens to my Verizon Dollars if I opt out?
Under section 7.4 of the program terms, all accumulated Verizon Dollars are forfeited immediately, except Dollars earned by Verizon Visa Card holders on eligible card spending.
Do I lose free activations and upgrades if I leave Verizon Dollars?
Yes. Section 7.4 says you "will lose access to waived fees for mobile device activations and/or upgrades." Verizon's launch announcement put those fees at up to $40 per device.
The terms say you may re-enroll at any time in the My Verizon app. They don't say a forfeited balance comes back.

headline: Hinge now uses OpenAI to analyze your chats, and may train its own models on your messages
tldr: Hinge's new Chat Insights runs your messages through OpenAI to make suggestions and personalize matches, and Hinge may train its models on them. There's a toggle in Settings.
who: Anyone who messages matches on Hinge, and the people they message, especially anyone who shares sensitive details (health, sexuality, location, plans to meet) in Hinge chat.
seo_title: Hinge Chat Insights: Hinge uses OpenAI on your messages. How to turn it off
seo_desc: Hinge's new help pages say Chat Insights uses OpenAI to look for patterns in your chats, and Hinge may use messages, sometimes raw, to train the models behind it. Settings > Chat Insights turns it off.

redline.after: Chat Insights helps us understand how your chats are going, so we can support you in the right moments. We use OpenAI to look for patterns and make suggestions that can help improve your experience.
redline.label: Help Center · What are Chat Insights? (new, Nov 9, 2026)
redline.note: Hinge's first OpenAI feature, Convo Starters, came with a promise that it does not process private messages. This one is built on them.

redline.after: This may include recommending other daters who we think better reflect your preferences, offering in-chat suggestions or feedback, tailoring features to your interests, or training the specific models behind these features.
redline.label: Help Center · How Does Hinge Use My Messages (new, Oct 28, 2026)
redline.note: Your messages can feed who Hinge shows you, and the models themselves.

redline.after: However, some use cases may require Hinge to process raw messages, which may include identifiable information or data considered sensitive under applicable law.
redline.label: Help Center · How Does Hinge Use My Messages
redline.note: Hinge says it will pseudonymize or de-identify "where possible", not always.

actions: To opt out, open Hinge, tap your photo icon, then Settings (the gear icon), scroll to Chat Insights and switch it off. Hinge's other page calls the same switch "Chat Insights for Personalization" in Account Settings
Check the switch even if you don't remember agreeing to anything: Hinge's pages don't say whether it starts on or off
Keep in mind that safety scanning and human review of chats aren't covered by the switch. Hinge says the only way to object to those is to delete your account
what:
Hinge has published two new help-center articles that describe a new use for your messages. "How Does Hinge Use My Messages" was created on October 28, 2026 and "What are Chat Insights?" on November 9, 2026, according to the help center's own timestamps. Both were last edited on November 13. Neither page existed in the Wayback Machine when we checked on November 14, and we found no news coverage.

## What Chat Insights does

The Chat Insights page says: "Chat Insights helps us understand how your chats are going, so we can support you in the right moments. We use OpenAI to look for patterns and make suggestions that can help improve your experience." It adds: "Hinge uses Chat Insights, but never shows them to other daters. Chat Insights improves Hinge over time. Patterns across conversations help us build features that make chatting feel easier."

The messages page explains what that personalization covers. "With your permission, we may also use the messages you send on Hinge to develop and test features designed to enable a more personalized experience for you on the app. This may include recommending other daters who we think better reflect your preferences, offering in-chat suggestions or feedback, tailoring features to your interests, or training the specific models behind these features."

It promises to keep the data to "the minimum necessary, including by pseudonymizing or de-identifying the messages where possible." Then it adds: "However, some use cases may require Hinge to process raw messages, which may include identifiable information or data considered sensitive under applicable law. If you'd rather this type of content never be used to personalize your experience, opting out is the simplest way to ensure that."

## Why it matters

Hinge's first OpenAI feature came with a different promise. When Convo Starters launched (Hinge newsroom, December 8, 2025), its help page said the feature uses only profile photos, Prompt answers and pronouns, and "Convo Starters do not analyze or otherwise process facial geometry, biometric data, or private messages." It also said OpenAI "cannot use the data to train its models, and deletes the data within 30 days of receipt." That page is still up. The Chat Insights pages name OpenAI, but they don't repeat those no-training and 30-day deletion terms or say whether they apply.

The pages also don't say whether Chat Insights starts switched on or off. "With your permission" suggests Hinge asks first, but neither page says how or when. Hinge's App Store release notes for its last two updates (10.12.1 and 10.12.2) only mention "performance improvements."

There's a second person in every chat. The messages page says: "Where and as legally required, Hinge will not process messages in a conversation unless all parties are opted in." That promise is limited to places where the law requires it. The page doesn't say what happens elsewhere when you have Chat Insights off and your match has it on.

Hinge's Privacy Policy (in effect since November 24, 2025, checked November 14) doesn't mention Chat Insights or OpenAI. It does already list "Developing and improving new features and services, including through machine learning" as a use of your data, and it counts "your chats with other members" among the content you share.

## What you can't turn off

The messages page lists uses of your chats that have no toggle: delivering them, "Safety and moderation: detecting harassment, scams, and other violations of our guidelines, whether by automated systems or human review", security, debugging, and aggregate analytics using de-identified or aggregated data. "If you object to Hinge's use of your messages for these purposes, you may delete your account." The Chat Insights page says turning the feature off "does not interfere with Hinge's safety processes."

## How other dating apps handle your messages

We checked what the other big dating apps say about AI and your chats (pages fetched November 14, 2026).

Grindr asks before training on chats. Its "Your Privacy & Artificial Intelligence at Grindr" help page counts "chat content" as special-category data and says: "You can choose whether or not to let Grindr use this type of data to train its AI technology. You'll see this option when you create your account." Its AI features, which include "summaries of previous interactions with other users" and "chat suggestions", are on "By default" until you opt out under "Enable gAI™ Features".

Bumble's Privacy Policy says it reviews "the content of messages sent in the App to identify topics, sentiments, and trends across our Users" after it will "take steps to remove personally identifying information from such messages, prior to reviewing them." It lists OpenAI as an AI provider for message prompts such as Icebreakers, noting OpenAI "only retains inputs and prompts for 30 days".

Tinder said in March 2026 that it gave its "Are You Sure?" and "Does This Bother You?" safety prompts "Large Language Model-powered upgrades" that read "tone and conversational nuance".

Hinge's pages say messages may be used, "With your permission", to train "the specific models behind these features", and that some uses "may require Hinge to process raw messages". Unlike Grindr's page, they don't say when or how that permission is asked. Unlike Hinge's own Convo Starters page and Bumble's policy, they don't state how long OpenAI keeps the data.

## What stays the same

Hinge says it "will never voluntarily share your messages with daters other than the intended recipients, nor with advertisers or other third-party companies aside from the approved service providers we engage to help us operate and improve the Hinge Service." You can still use chat with Chat Insights off.

What you can do: open Hinge, tap your photo icon, then Settings (the gear icon), scroll down to Chat Insights and toggle it off. The messages page calls the same switch "Chat Insights for Personalization" in Account Settings.

faq: Does Hinge use OpenAI on my messages?

For Chat Insights, yes. Hinge's help page says: "We use OpenAI to look for patterns and make suggestions that can help improve your experience." Hinge says the insights are never shown to other daters.
How do I turn off Chat Insights on Hinge?

Tap your photo icon, then Settings (gear icon), scroll to Chat Insights and toggle it off. Hinge's messages page calls it "Chat Insights for Personalization" in Account Settings. You can still use chat with it off.
Can Hinge train AI on my messages?

Hinge's own models, yes, if Chat Insights is on: its help page lists "training the specific models behind these features" as a use. The Chat Insights pages don't say whether OpenAI may keep or train on the data. For the older Convo Starters feature, Hinge said OpenAI can't train on the data and deletes it within 30 days.
Does turning off Chat Insights stop Hinge from scanning my chats?
No. Safety and moderation (automated and human review), security, debugging and aggregate analytics have no toggle. Hinge says if you object to those, you can delete your account.
Do other dating apps use AI on your messages?

Yes, in different ways. Grindr says you choose at sign-up whether it can train AI on chat content, but its AI features (including chat summaries) are on by default. Bumble reviews message content for topics and trends after removing personal details, and uses OpenAI for Icebreakers with 30-day retention. Tinder uses large language models in its "Are You Sure?" safety prompts.
